phoenixAngle.heading: Why Quality Valves & Line Flushing Matter in Phoenix
paragraphs: When installing a new faucet in Phoenix, disturbing old under-sink shutoff valves or shutting down main water lines often shakes loose flakes of hard-water calcium scale from interior copper walls. If supply lines are not flushed thoroughly before the new faucet aerator and pull-down cartridge are connected, that scale packs tightly behind fine ceramic screens and causes immediate low flow.

Upgrading old plastic-stem shutoff valves to full-port brass quarter-turn ball stops during fixture installation ensures you have dependable local emergency shutoffs that will not seize up from Valley mineral deposits or leak unexpectedly inside vanity cabinets.

facts.text: Phoenix hard water mineral deposits contribute to aerator clogging and valve seizing across residential fixtures.

faqs.q: Can a plumber install a kitchen faucet I bought online or at a store?
faqs.a: Yes. Most Phoenix homeowners pick out their own kitchen, bathroom, or laundry faucet to match their decor. We bring all necessary mounting basin tools, new braided supply lines, and brass shutoff valves to complete the installation cleanly and without leaks.

faqs.q: How do I know what hole configuration my sink has?
faqs.a: Look under or above the sink rim: a single hole is standard for pull-down spouts; 3 holes spaced 4 inches apart fit a centerset faucet; and 3 holes spaced 8 inches apart fit a widespread faucet. Many single-hole faucets include an optional deck plate to cover extra holes.

faqs.q: Why should I replace under-sink shutoff valves when installing a faucet?
faqs.a: Older multi-turn valves with rubber washers frequently stick open, seize, or weep from the packing nut once touched. Replacing them with modern brass quarter-turn ball valves gives you dependable local shutoffs whenever future maintenance or fixture swaps are needed down the road.

faqs.q: Why does my new faucet have weak water pressure right after being installed?
faqs.a: Disturbing water lines during installation almost always dislodges loose mineral scale inside older copper pipes. That grit gets trapped in the aerator screen or cartridge inlet; removing the aerator, thoroughly flushing the lines, and rinsing the screen restores full household pressure.

faqs.q: Does installing a new faucet require a city permit in Phoenix?
faqs.a: Rules differ by city and by the specific work being done. Under City of Phoenix residential permit guidelines, replacing existing faucets and fixtures in the same location does not require a permit, whereas adding brand-new plumbing rough-ins or moving lines does.

faqs.q: Do you install bathroom sink pop-up drain assemblies with the faucet?
faqs.a: Yes. Most bathroom faucet sets include a matching pop-up drain assembly. We remove the old corroded drain flange, seal the new one with 100% silicone or plumber's putty, and test the basin overflow through multiple cycles for leak-free drainage in your bathroom.
